verdict: Service in the focus hours is significantly worse than the baseline on late_share.

evidence: [F] 99% of late trains were already late at Smith-9 Sts (inherited delay). Origins: at or before East Broadway: 78, at Smith-9 Sts: 4, at or before Bergen St: 3, at or before Jay St-MetroTech: 2. Largest time loss on segment York St -> Jay St-MetroTech (median +35s vs schedule).
[F] 89% of headway gaps at the target already existed at Smith-9 Sts.
[G] 96% of late trains were already late at Smith-9 Sts (inherited delay). Origins: at or before Clinton-Washington Avs: 15, at or before Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts: 3, at Fulton St: 2, at Carroll St: 2.
[G] 85% of headway gaps at the target already existed at Smith-9 Sts.
53% of hours with problems ran fewer than 90% of scheduled trains (overall service delivered 81%): cancellations or missing trips are creating gaps.
[G] Trains that would arrive at Bergen St within 180s behind a F train lose 59s more there than others (p=0.000; 38% of trips affected); 43% of problem arrivals at the target had such a conflict.
Weekend problem rate is 1.9x the weekday rate; weekend service changes / planned work likely.
21% of problem arrivals occurred during planned service changes (lift 0.9x).
MTA reports 'Planned ROW Work' as 36% of delays on line(s) F, G (1.2x the system share) in the analysed months.
ETAs for problem arrivals drifted 167s on average vs 98s otherwise (1.7x): trains are being held or re-dispatched upstream.
10% of problem arrivals happened while an MTA 'signal' alert was active for the line (problem rate 40% with an alert vs 26% without, lift 1.5x).
MTA reports 'Infrastructure & Equipment' as 36% of delays on line(s) F, G (1.2x the system share) in the analysed months.
MTA reports 'Police & Medical' as 16% of delays on line(s) F, G (0.7x the system share) in the analysed months.

recommendations.action: Fill cancelled trips on F, G during 06:00-07:00, 11:00-12:00, 13:00-14:00, 14:00-15:00: check crew availability and car assignments
recommendations.rationale: Fewer trains than scheduled are running in the problem hours.
recommendations.expected_effect: Restores scheduled headways; largest APT lever available.

recommendations.action: Review merge priority and dispatch spacing at Bergen St, where F trains run ahead of G trains bound for 4 Av-9 St
recommendations.rationale: Arrivals following a train of another route are disproportionately delayed.
recommendations.expected_effect: Fewer merge conflicts; smoother headways for both services.

recommendations.action: Check weekend / late-night planned service changes for F, G; use alternates other lines at the station
recommendations.rationale: Planned work is announced in advance.

recommendations.action: Adjust the schedule so F and G slots are offset by at least half a headway at Bergen St
recommendations.expected_effect: Structural fix that survives day-to-day variability.

recommendations.action: Review the general-order (planned work) schedule for F, G; add supplement trains or move work windows off 06:00-07:00, 11:00-12:00, 13:00-14:00, 14:00-15:00
recommendations.rationale: Problems coincide with planned service changes.
recommendations.expected_effect: Planned changes stop degrading the analysed hours.

recommendations.action: Set a gap-filling rule: dispatch the next available train from Jamaica-179 St when a gap over 11 min forms
recommendations.rationale: A fifth of arrivals follow a large gap.
recommendations.expected_effect: Caps the longest waits, which dominate the APT metric.

recommendations.action: Review dispatcher holding practice upstream of 4 Av-9 St; consider publishing hold reasons in the feed
recommendations.rationale: ETAs drift substantially before problem arrivals, indicating holds.
recommendations.expected_effect: Fewer discretionary holds; more accurate countdown clocks.
